title: LOT Polish Airlines 5055
summary: An Ilyushin Il-62 climbing to cruise altitude experienced catastrophic failure of the number 2 engine due to faulty bearings with insufficient rollers. The bearing reached 1000 degrees Celsius, the engine shaft disintegrated, and the turbine disc exploded. Debris severed flight controls and caused fire that destroyed all flight-control systems.
probable_cause: Bearing failure in number 2 engine due to manufacturing defect: rollers were reduced from 26 to 13 per bearing due to supply delays, causing shaft disintegration and turbine disc explosion.

factors.evidence: Manufacturing defect in bearings went undetected: bearings were fitted with only 13 rollers instead of 26.
Number 2 engine bearing reached 1000 degrees Celsius nine minutes after maximum thrust applied.
Debris from explosion violently spread, puncturing fuselage and severing flight controls and electrical cables.
Debris burst into cargo hold causing rapidly spreading fire in adjoining number 1 engine.
All flight-control systems were destroyed by spreading fire, resulting in loss of control.

events.text: Aircraft took off from runway 33 at Warsaw and was cleared to climb to 31000 feet.
ATC instructed aircraft to climb to 18000 ft as quickly as possible; crew applied maximum thrust on engines.
Nine minutes after maximum thrust applied, number 2 engine faulty bearings reached 1000 degrees Celsius and exploded near Lipinki at 8200 m altitude.
Freed turbine disc exploded at high speed; debris punctured fuselage, severed flight controls, caused fire destroying all flight-control systems.

notes: bearing manufacturing defect was root cause
deadliest accident involving Ilyushin Il-62 at time

title: Philippine Airlines 206
summary: Philippine Airlines Flight 206, a Hawker Siddeley HS 748, crashed onto the fog-shrouded slopes of Mount Ugu on June 26, 1987 during approach to Baguio. As the plane approached Baguio City, the pilot reported poor visibility. A monsoon was also reported in the area. Flight 206 disappeared from radar screens around ten minutes before landing. All 50 passengers and crew members perished in the crash at 180 meters below the summit.

title: South African Airways 295
summary: South African Airways Flight 295 experienced a catastrophic in-flight fire in the cargo area during approach to Mauritius on November 28, 1987. The fire destroyed the aircraft's electrical systems, resulting in loss of communication and control. The aircraft broke apart mid-air and crashed into the Indian Ocean, killing all 159 passengers and crew on board.
probable_cause: An in-flight fire of undetermined origin started in the cargo section on the main deck, destroying electrical systems and aircraft control capability before impact, though the specific source of ignition could not be definitively determined.

factors.evidence: A fire started in the cargo section on the main deck which was probably not extinguished before impact.
The fire began in the cargo section and a charred fire extinguisher was recovered from wreckage with molten metal and melted cargo netting.
The fire began to destroy the aircraft's important electrical systems and the tail section broke off first when the fire began to burn the structure of the aircraft.
The smoke evacuation checklist calls for depressurization and opening cabin doors, though no direct evidence exists that it was followed or that crew attempted to fight the fire in cargo hold.
The main deck cargo compartment configuration on the 747 Combi permitted mixing of passengers and cargo with potential fire hazards.

events.text: Fire started in cargo section on main deck at some point during landing approach to Mauritius.
Last communication with Mauritius air traffic control was received.
Aircraft broke apart mid-air, tail section breaking off first when fire burned aircraft structure.
Air traffic control formally declared the aircraft missing after 36 minutes of lost contact.

notes: Cause of fire origin could not be definitively determined
Multiple conflicting theories about ignition source

title: Korean Air 858
summary: Boeing 707 operated a scheduled international passenger flight from Baghdad to Seoul with stopovers in Abu Dhabi and Bangkok. Two North Korean agents, Kim Sung-Il and Kim Hyon-hui, traveled with the aircraft from Baghdad to Abu Dhabi under false Japanese passports. In the aircraft cabin, they planted a Panasonic transistor radio containing explosives with a detonator and liquid explosive intensifier above their seats in rows 7B and 7C. They disembarked at Abu Dhabi while other passengers continued. On the second leg from Abu Dhabi to Bangkok, near the end of the flight over the Andaman Sea, the bomb detonated causing explosive decompression and structural failure of the aircraft. The aircraft crashed into the Andaman Sea killing all 104 passengers and 11 crew members aboard.
probable_cause: Deliberate bombing by North Korean agents acting on orders from the North Korean government to destroy the aircraft as part of political-military operations. Kim Jong Il was identified as ultimately responsible for the bombing.

factors.evidence: bomb was planted inside an overhead storage bin in the airplane's passenger cabin by two North Korean agents who deliberately detonated the device
the bomb was not detected by airport security or cargo screening procedures at Baghdad or Abu Dhabi
the bomb detonated and destroyed the aircraft in mid-air over the Andaman Sea
the aircraft was destroyed and broke apart over the Andaman Sea 18 miles west of the Burmese coast

title: 1987 Alianza Lima air disaster
summary: A Fokker F27-400M chartered by Peruvian football club Alianza Lima crashed into the Pacific Ocean seven miles from Jorge Chávez International Airport near Callao on December 8, 1987. Upon lowering the landing gear during descent, the nose gear did not display a green light. The copilot had poor foreign language skills and misread the English-language procedure. A visual check confirmed the nose gear appeared down. However, while over water the aircraft flew too low and the right wing struck the ocean surface as the aircraft lined up with the runway. Only the pilot survived the initial crash. Of 43 occupants, 42 perished. The investigation cited the pilot's poor night-flying experience, the copilot's misinterpretation of emergency procedures, and the aircraft's poor mechanical condition as contributing factors.
probable_cause: Pilot's lack of night-flying experience, copilot's misinterpretation of English-language emergency procedures for the landing gear issue, and aircraft's poor mechanical condition contributed to the accident.
